ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of the semicircle $O$, and $C$ is a point on the semicircle $O$. Connect $AC$ and $CB$, where $D$ is a point on the arc $\widehat{BC}$, and connect $CD$ and $BD$. If $\angle ABC=40^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle D$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB$ is the diameter of semicircle O,\\
it follows that $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle ABC=40^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle CAB=50^\circ$,\\
since the quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in semicircle O,\\
it follows that $\angle D=180^\circ-50^\circ=\boxed{130^\circ}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a horizontal diameter AB, O is on AB, and the upper semicircle with AB as diameter is drawn. Point C is located at the upper left of the upper semicircle, and point D is located at the upper right of the upper semicircle, on arc BC. In the figure, AC, CB, CD, and BD are connected. The required ∠D is the angle formed by DC and DB, namely ∠CDB. Then reason: It is known that ∠ABC = 40°. ∠ABC is an inscribed angle, and the measure of arc AC that it subtends is 2 × 40° = 80°. Because AB is a diameter, the measure of the semicircular arc AB on the other side is 180°. Point D is on arc BC, so ∠CDB intercepts arc CB that does not contain D, that is, the arc from C through A and then to B, whose measure is arc CA + semicircular arc AB = 80° + 180° = 260°. An inscribed angle is equal to half the measure of the arc it subtends, so ∠CDB = 260° ÷ 2 = 130°.
